attack_method: Compromised single legacy VPN account credentials (without MFA); DarkSide ransomware deployment encrypting billing and business systems.
consequences: Precautionary 5-day shutdown of 5,500 miles of fuel pipeline supplying 45% of East Coast fuel; airline flight disruptions; regional fuel panic and gas station shortages; emergency declaration by US DOT.
financial_losses: $4.4 million ransom paid (75 Bitcoin, ~$2.3M later recovered by FBI) + estimated tens of millions in operational downtime and forensic investigation.
financial_status: Verified: CEO Joseph Blount testified to US Senate confirming $4.4M ransom payment.
sources: US Senate Homeland Security & Governmental Affairs Committee Hearing (June 2021)
US Department of Justice Press Release (June 7, 2021)
CISA Alert AA21-131A

attack_method: WannaCry worm exploiting EternalBlue (SMBv1 vulnerability MS17-010) spreading autonomously across unpatched Windows systems.
consequences: Disrupted 80 out of 236 NHS England hospital trusts; cancelled an estimated 19,000 medical appointments and surgeries; ambulances diverted from emergency rooms; staff reverted to paper records.
financial_losses: Estimated £92 million total cost (£19M in direct IT remediation and lost output during disruption + £73M in subsequent IT modernization and cybersecurity upgrades).
financial_status: Verified: Official UK Department of Health and Social Care evaluation report (2018).
sources: UK National Audit Office (NAO) Report: Investigation WannaCry cyber attack and the NHS (Oct 2017)
UK Department of Health and Social Care Securing Cyber Resilience in Health and Care Report (2018)

attack_method: Supply chain compromise of Ukrainian accounting software M.E.Doc; weaponized wiper disguised as ransomware spreading via EternalBlue and PsExec.
consequences: Complete shutdown of Maersk's global booking system across 76 port terminals; 45,000 PCs, 4,000 servers, and 2,500 applications reinstalled from scratch; container ships stranded at sea.
financial_losses: Approximately $250 million to $300 million in direct lost revenue, demurrage fees, and disaster recovery costs.
financial_status: Verified: Formally reported in Maersk Q3 2017 and Annual Financial Statements.
sources: A.P. Møller - Mærsk A/S Annual Report 2017
Wired: The Untold Story of NotPetya, the Most Devastating Cyberattack in History (2018)
White House Statement on NotPetya Attribution (Feb 2018)

incident_name: Dyn DNS Mirai Botnet DDoS Attack
attack_method: Distributed Denial of Service orchestrated by Mirai botnet compromising ~100,000 IoT devices (DVRs, IP cameras) using factory-default telnet credentials, generating 1.2 Tbps of SYN and DNS traffic.
consequences: Widespread outages across North America and Europe for major platforms including GitHub, Twitter, Spotify, Netflix, Reddit, Amazon, PayPal, and PlayStation Network for over 10 hours.
financial_losses: Dyn estimated loss was undisclosed; overall economic loss across affected online businesses estimated at $110 million (IHS Markit estimate).
financial_status: Estimated: Direct ransom was not sought; loss derived from industry downtime analytics.
sources: Dyn Official Analysis of the 21 October 2016 DDoS Attack
US Department of Justice Indictment: United States v. Jha et al. (Mirai Authors)
IHS Markit Cyber Risk Analytics Report (2016)

attack_method: Memcached UDP reflection amplification attack reaching 1.35 Tbps and 126.9 million packets per second without using a compromised botnet.
consequences: GitHub was intermittently unavailable for 8 minutes; automated Akamai Prolexic routed and absorbed the volumetric spike, restoring service in under 10 minutes.
financial_losses: $0 ransom paid; minimal financial impact due to pre-provisioned Tier-1 DDoS mitigation scrubbing centers.
financial_status: Verified: Confirmed by GitHub Engineering Incident Post-Mortem.
sources: GitHub Engineering: Incident Report: 1.35 Tbps Memcached Amplification DDoS (March 2018)
Akamai Technologies Threat Research: Memcached Reflection DDoS Analysis

attack_method: Exploitation of unpatched Apache Struts CVE-2017-5638 vulnerability in dispute resolution web portal; attacker traversed internal databases for 76 days undetected.
consequences: Exfiltration of sensitive personal credit records of 147 million consumers, including names, Social Security numbers, birth dates, home addresses, and 209,000 credit card numbers.
financial_losses: Over $1.38 billion total costs, including $425 million FTC consumer redress fund settlement, $100 million CFPB civil penalties, and hundreds of millions in forensic legal upgrades.
financial_status: Verified: Federal Trade Commission (FTC) & Consumer Financial Protection Bureau Settlement Order (2019).
sources: Federal Trade Commission (FTC): Equifax Data Breach Settlement (2019)
US Government Accountability Office (GAO-18-559): Actions Taken by Equifax and Federal Agencies
US House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform: The Equifax Data Breach Majority Staff Report

attack_method: State-sponsored (APT29/Cozy Bear) software supply chain injection of backdoor into Orion IT monitoring platform updates (SUNBURST / Solorigate DLL).
consequences: Trojanized updates delivered to approximately 18,000 public and private organizations worldwide, leading to high-profile espionage breaches at US Departments of Homeland Security, Treasury, State, and Energy.
financial_losses: SolarWinds reported $50+ million in direct cyber response expenses and a $26 million SEC shareholder derivative settlement; wider national enterprise remediation costs exceeded $500 million.
financial_status: Verified: SolarWinds SEC Form 10-K Filings & CISA Emergency Directive 21-01.
sources: CISA Emergency Directive 21-01: Mitigate SolarWinds Orion Code Compromise
FireEye / Mandiant Cyber Threat Intelligence: Highly Evasive Attacker Leverages SolarWinds Supply Chain
SolarWinds Form 10-K SEC Annual Report (2021)

incident_name: FACC AG CEO Fraud Business Email Compromise (BEC)
attack_method: Spear-phishing and executive impersonation (Whaling / BEC) spoofing the CEO's email address to instruct an accounting employee to transfer funds for a fake acquisition.
consequences: Employee wired company funds to foreign bank accounts over several transactions; the company's CEO and CFO were subsequently fired by the supervisory board.
financial_losses: €54 million ($61 million) stolen; €10.8 million ($12.2 million) seized and recovered via international police cooperation; net loss ~€42.8 million ($48.8 million).
financial_status: Verified: FACC AG Ad-hoc Public Disclosures & Austrian Stock Market Filings.
sources: FACC AG Corporate Ad-hoc Disclosure (Jan 19, 2016)
Reuters: Austrian plane parts maker FACC fires CEO after $56 million cyber fraud (May 2016)

incident_name: Heartland Payment Systems SQL Injection Card Theft
attack_method: SQL Injection on corporate web login page allowed attackers (Albert Gonzalez gang) to gain access and place a packet sniffer directly on the internal card processing network.
consequences: Theft of more than 130 million debit and credit card numbers from over 250,000 businesses processing transactions through Heartland; Visa and Mastercard temporarily revoked Heartland's processing certification.
financial_losses: Over $140 million paid in settlements to Visa, MasterCard, American Express, and issuing banks, alongside legal and compliance fees.
financial_status: Verified: US Department of Justice Indictment & Heartland SEC Filings.
sources: US Department of Justice Press Release: Albert Gonzalez Indicted for Heartland Breach (Aug 2009)
Heartland Payment Systems Form 8-K SEC Filing
Federal Reserve Bank of Boston Risk Study: Payment Cards and the Heartland Breach

attack_method: Blind SQL injection targeting an outdated legacy web server acquired during an acquisition (Tiscali UK) using automated vulnerability scanners.
consequences: Personal data of 156,959 customers and 15,656 bank account numbers exfiltrated; customer churn of 101,000 subscribers; massive brand erosion.
financial_losses: £400,000 fine from UK Information Commissioner's Office (record fine at the time) + £42 million in direct trading impact and £18 million in security upgrades (total £60M+).
financial_status: Verified: UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) Enforcement Notice & TalkTalk Financial Reports.
sources: UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) Penalty Notice against TalkTalk Telecom Group PLC (Oct 2016)
TalkTalk Interim Financial Results 2015/2016

incident_name: British Airways Magecart Digital Skimming (XSS / Supply Chain)
attack_method: Client-side script injection (Magecart digital skimming) through modified baggage claim JavaScript code on the website and mobile app, harvesting checkout payment details in real time.
consequences: Exfiltration of personal and payment data of approximately 429,612 customers and staff (including CVV security codes and billing addresses).
financial_losses: £20 million ($26 million) ICO GDPR penalty (reduced from initial £183 million proposal due to COVID-19 sector considerations) + multi-million pound confidential class-action lawsuit settlement.
financial_status: Verified: UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) Final Penalty Notice (Oct 2020).
sources: UK Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) Penalty Notice: British Airways PLC (2020)
RiskIQ Threat Research: Inside the Magecart British Airways Breach

attack_method: Intrusion into Dutch CA web servers yielding unauthorized issuance of over 500 fraudulent wildcard SSL/TLS certificates (including *.google.com) used for active Iranian government MitM interception.
consequences: Interception and eavesdropping of communications of ~300,000 Iranian users attempting to access Google and Gmail; total revocation of trust by Microsoft, Google, Mozilla, and Apple; bankruptcy of DigiNotar.
financial_losses: 100% loss of business resulting in total company liquidation and bankruptcy declared within two months of discovery.
financial_status: Verified: Dutch Government Fox-IT Investigation Report & Haarlem Commercial Court Bankruptcy.
sources: Fox-IT Black Tulip Report: Operation Black Tulip - Certificate Authority DigiNotar Compromised (Sept 2011)
Dutch Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations Official Inquiry

incident_name: 23andMe Credential Stuffing & Sensitive DNA Data Leak
attack_method: Automated credential stuffing using username/password pairs leaked in past third-party breaches without MFA enforcement; leveraged the 'DNA Relatives' feature to scrape millions of connected profile trees.
consequences: Compromised direct accounts of 14,000 users, leading to the scraping of ancestry and sensitive health genetic metadata of 6.9 million total individuals; data posted on hacking forums with targeted ethnic filtering.
financial_losses: $30 million tentative class action settlement fund in 2024 + severe stock decline and restructuring.
financial_status: Verified: 23andMe SEC Form 8-K and US District Court Northern District of California filings.
sources: 23andMe Form 8-K SEC Filing (Dec 2023)
US District Court Northern District of California Class Action Settlement Proceedings (2024)
CISA / FBI Joint Cybersecurity Advisory on Credential Stuffing

attack_method: Sophisticated military-grade worm using 4 zero-day Windows exploits, air-gap bridging via infected USB flash drives, and targeted Siemens Step7 PLC code modification.
consequences: Physical destruction of approximately 1,000 IR-1 gas centrifuges by altering rotor speeds while spoofing normal industrial telemetry back to operators; set back Iranian nuclear program by an estimated 1-2 years.
financial_losses: Estimated tens to hundreds of millions in specialized nuclear enrichment centrifuges and facility reconstruction (no exact state budget disclosed).
financial_status: Estimated: Classified military operation; physical destruction confirmed by IAEA inspection reports.
sources: Symantec Security Response: W32.Stuxnet Dossier (Feb 2011)
International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) Safeguards Reports on Iran (2010-2011)
Kim Zetter: Countdown to Zero Day - Stuxnet and the Launch of the World's First Digital Weapon
